subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a core compaction lifecycle contract that lets agents receive early warnings, write a structured handoff checkpoint, and request bounded deferral, and what authority may survive that boundary?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but implementing it changes public config, session-state semantics, compaction timing, tool authority, and approval continuity, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Design Core Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Approve a design-first core contract for warning events, checkpoint fields, deferral governance, audit logging, and resume validation before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Surfaces
options.body: Limit near-term work to improving notifyUser, memoryFlush, hooks, and checkpoint docs without adding agent deferral or authority-carrying resume semantics.

options.title: Fold Into Broad Transparency Tracker
options.body: Move this into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58830 if maintainers want all compaction UX and confirmation mechanisms owned by one umbrella design.

recommendation.title: Design Core Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a design-first core contract for warning events, checkpoint fields, deferral governance, audit logging, and resume validation before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for memoryFlush and core compaction product direction points to steipete, and the blocker is a product/security boundary choice.
